Notes: Refer to the "Footnotes" section of this press release.  Certain totals, subtotals and percentages may not reconcile due to rounding.
"We continue to proactively manage the business in a challenging market environment for quality-biased, high-conviction active managers while maintaining our commitment to long-term value creation
," said Maxime Ménard, Global President and Chief Executive Officer.

"We are broadening our range of return drivers, including core and quantitative investment strategies, while remaining focused on building a more streamlined, stronger, and more accountable organization through disciplined capital allocation, effective governance, and clear alignment with the long-term interests of our clients and shareholders."
"Our cost management initiatives and ongoing focus on expense discipline continue to offset softer year-to-date revenues"
said Lucas Pontillo, Executive Director, Global Chief Financial Officer and Head of Corporate Strategy.

"We also reduced net debt by $34 million in the quarter, in line with the first pillar of our strategic plan of creating greater balance sheet capacity. In keeping with this, Management has decided to take prudent proactive steps to further accelerate progress against this priority. As such, Management has recommended, and the Board has approved, the discontinuation of the quarterly dividend."

Total AUM of $151.4 billion decreased by $12.1 billion or 7.4% compared to June 30, 2026. The decrease reflects net outflows from Public Markets of $7.7 billion, mostly from sub-advised AUM, and unfavourable market impact of $3.8 billion, mainly from Fixed Income strategies reflecting rising interest rates during the quarter.

Within Public Markets, directly managed AUM of $104.7 billion decreased $5.7 billion or 5.2% reflecting adverse market impact of $3.1 billion and net outflows of $2.5 billion, primarily from net outflows within Canadian Large Cap Equity strategies.

Sub-advised AUM of $24.7 billion decreased $6.1 billion, primarily due to net outflows of $3.0 billion related to ongoing client relationships and $2.2 billion of lost mandates. Lost mandates include approximately $1.5 billion of AUM which transferred directly to PineStone, as previously announced.

Private Markets AUM of $21.9 billion decreased by $0.4 billion or 1.8%, primarily due to net outflows of $0.6 billion, reflecting a client's decision to insource management of a real estate mandate in the UK along with return of capital.
Average AUM decreased by $6.8 billion or 4.2% and reflects the timing of outflows and market impacts.

AUM decreased by $12.7 billion or 7.7% compared to December 31, 2025, primarily due to net outflows from Public Markets of $16.6 billion, mostly from sub-advised AUM, and the wind down of the Canadian Equity Small Cap Core strategy in the first quarter which reduced AUM by $0.7 billion. These decreases were partly offset by a favourable market and foreign exchange impact of $5.3 billion.

Within Public Markets, directly managed AUM decreased $3.5 billion or 3.2%, reflecting net outflows of $5.6 billion, mainly from Equity strategies, and the wind down of the Canadian Equity Small Cap Core strategy, partly offset by positive market impact of $2.8 billion.

Sub-advised AUM decreased $9.3 billion due to lost mandates of $5.9 billion and net outflows of $5.1 billion related to ongoing client relationships, partly offset by a positive market impact of $1.8 billion. Of the $5.9 billion of lost mandates, $4.2 billion related to large Institutional and Financial Intermediaries clients that, to our knowledge, transferred their AUM directly to PineStone.
Private Markets AUM remained largely flat as net outflows of $0.6 billion were offset by positive market and foreign exchange impacts.

Revenues of $150.4 million decreased by $4.7 million or 3.0% compared to Q2 2026, primarily from lower base management fees from sub-advised mandates and lower performance fees, partly offset by an increase in share of earnings in joint ventures and associates. Revenues decreased by $16.7 million or 10.0% compared to Q3 2025, primarily due to lower base management fees from sub-advised mandates, and lower performance fees.

SG&A expenses of $106.6 million decreased by $11.0 million or 9.4% compared to Q2 2026, primarily due to lower employee compensation costs, travel and marketing expenses, and sub-advisory fees. SG&A expenses decreased by $15.9 million or 13.0% compared to Q3 2025, primarily due to lower employee compensation costs, continued cost optimization initiatives, as well as lower sub-advisory fees. SG&A expenses, excluding share-based compensation, were $107.4 million, a decrease of $5.7 million or 5.0% compared to Q2 2026 and a decrease of $9.4 million or 8.1% compared to Q3 2025.

During the current quarter, $3.3 million of share-based compensation expense and $2.8 million of variable compensation costs previously recognized were reversed. These reversals were due to changes in the Canadian Large Cap Equity team, as previously announced, and the departure of certain employees.

Adjusted EBITDA of $42.9 million increased by $0.9 million or 2.1% compared to Q2 2026 due to a decrease in SG&A expenses, excluding share-based compensation, partly offset by lower revenues. Adjusted EBITDA decreased by $7.4 million or 14.7% compared to Q3 2025 due to lower revenues partly offset by lower SG&A expense, excluding share-based compensation.

Adjusted net earnings of $23.9 million remained in-line compared to Q2 2026. Adjusted net earnings decreased by $1.1 million or 4.4% compared to Q3 2025, primarily due to lower revenues, partly offset by lower SG&A expenses, excluding share-based compensation, interest on long-term debt and debentures and income tax expense.
Net earnings attributable to the Company's shareholders of $6.7 million increased by $3.2 million or 91.4% compared to Q2 2026 and increased by $0.9 million or 15.5% compared to Q3 2025.

LTM free cash flow of $90.2 million decreased by $2.7 million or 2.9% compared to Q2 2026. The decrease was primarily due to higher interest paid on long-term debt and debentures combined with higher dividends paid to non-controlling interest, partly offset by higher distributions received from joint ventures and associates. LTM free cash flow increased by $3.1 million or 3.6% compared to Q3 2025, primarily due to lower lease payments combined with lower interest paid on long term debt and debentures, partly offset by higher dividends paid to non-controlling interest.

Net debt decreased by $34 million during the quarter to $689 million at the end of Q3 2026, and Net debt ratio of 3.8x was unchanged over the same period. Net debt increased by $10 million compared to the end of Q3 2025, and Net debt ratio increased to 3.8x from 3.5x over the same period.
The Company did not repurchase shares during the quarter.

Revenues of $458.8 million decreased by $34.1 million or 6.9% from the corresponding period of 2025, primarily due to lower base management fees in Public Markets mainly from sub-advised mandates, lower performance fees, and lower share of earnings in joint ventures and associates. These decreases were partly offset by higher base management fees from directly managed AUM.

SG&A expenses of $338.3 million decreased by $28.6 million or 7.8% from the corresponding period of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to lower employee compensation costs related to continued cost optimization initiatives, and lower sub-advisory fees. During the current quarter, $3.3 million of share-based compensation expense and $2.8 million of variable compensation costs previously recognized were reversed. These reversals were due to changes in the Canadian Large Cap Equity team, as previously announced, and the departure of certain employees. SG&A expenses, excluding share-based compensation, were $331.2 million, a decrease of $22.3 million or 6.3% compared to the corresponding period of 2025.

Adjusted EBITDA of $127.7 million decreased by $11.7 million or 8.4% from the corresponding period of 2025, primarily due to lower revenues, partly offset by lower SG&A expenses, excluding share-based compensation.

Adjusted net earnings of $71.3 million decreased by $6.4 million or 8.2% from the corresponding period of 2025, primarily due to lower revenues, partly offset by lower SG&A expenses, excluding share-based compensation, and lower interest on long-term debt and debentures.

Net earnings attributable to the Company's shareholders of $13.1 million decreased $18.3 million or 58.3% from the corresponding period of 2025.  Prior year results included a $12.7 million gain on revaluation of an investment related to the acquisition of a controlling interest in a real estate investment platform. In addition, lower revenues were partly offset by lower SG&A as well as additional earnings of $0.8 million from the Company acquiring the remaining 25% interest in Fiera Infrastructure Inc, on April 20, 2026.
The Company purchased and cancelled 691,605 Class A Shares for total consideration of $3.9 million.

On November 11, 2026, the Company's Board of Directors discontinued the quarterly dividend. The decision reflects the Company's current capital allocation priorities and its focus on maintaining financial flexibility, including reducing leverage. The Board of Directors will continue to assess the Company's capital allocation priorities on an ongoing basis.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization ("EBITDA"), Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA margin, Adjusted net earnings, Adjusted EPS (diluted), Free cash flow, Last Twelve Months ("LTM") free cash flow, SG&A expense, excluding share-based compensation, Net debt and Net debt ratio are not standardized measures prescribed by International Financial Reporting Standards ("IFRS"), and are therefore unlikely to be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. We have included non-IFRS measures to provide investors with supplemental measures of our operating and financial performance. We believe non-IFRS measures are important supplemental metrics of operating and financial performance because they highlight trends in our core business that may not otherwise be apparent when relying solely on IFRS measures. Securities analysts, investors and other interested parties frequently use non-IFRS measures in the evaluation of issuers, many of which present non-IFRS measures when reporting their results. Management also uses non-IFRS measures in order to facilitate operating and financial performance comparisons from period to period, to prepare annual budgets and to assess its ability to meet future debt service, capital expenditure and working capital requirements.

For a description of the Company's non-IFRS measures, please refer to page 52 of the Company's Management's Discussion and Analysis for the Three and Nine-Month Periods ended September 30, 2026 which is available on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.
